**Day 0 \- Wednesday 14th October**

**Hotel \-** 

**Travelodge Gatwick Airport Central**

Povey Cross Road, Gatwick, RH6 0BE

### **How to get to your hotel**

### Leave the M23 at Junction 9, signposted for Gatwick Airport. Go straight through the first roundabout (signposted Redhill A23) and then at the next roundabout take the 4th exit towards Redhill A23. At the next roundabout take the first exit past the Esso service station and turn on to Povey Cross Road. The Travelodge is located on the left hand side. 

North terminal pick-up point is outside the terminal from the Pick-Up zone. Gatwick Hoppa buses also provide a regular shuttle service to and from the airport. £5.25 per adult.

![][image2]

**Parking \-** 

Gatwick Holiday Parking is located on Larkins Road, close to London Gatwick's North Terminal  
Once at the North Terminal, please follow road signs to Gatwick Holiday Parking  
From the direction of London or Brighton, exit the M23 at Junction 9  
At the first roundabout, follow signs for the North Terminal  
At the second roundabout, continue straight towards the Long Stay car parks  
Go past the Shell petrol station and follow the road signs to Gatwick Holiday Parking

**Do not enter the Official London Gatwick Airport Long Stay car park by mistake as you may be charged extra. At the Long Stay entrance roundabout simply continue to follow the road signage to Gatwick Holiday Parking, which is a further 0.6 miles ahead.** 

![][image3]

Free shuttle buses run every 15 minutes from the car park and take around 7 minutes to reach the North Terminal  
**North Terminal**  
Drop-off (departure): Bus stop 10  
Pick-up (return): Bus stop 3

**Day 2 – Friday 16th October | Land and Explore**

Land at Terminal 1, South Wing. Wait for Jack to arrive at 14:30. 

**Welcome Suica Card**  
Can get one from B1F floor in the airport. Welcome Suica can be purchased at Welcome Suica vending machines, JR EAST Travel Service Center, JAPAN RAIL CAFÉ, and TAKANAWA GATEWAY Travel Service Center.The card’s validity period is 28 days, including the date of purchase.  
Top up your card at Seven Bank ATMs, found at 7-Eleven and at other convenience stores.  
ONLY CASH \- CANT TOP UP WITH CARD  
Can use it like an Oyster for transport, in shops and for vending machines.  
![][image7]

**Bus to Tokyo**  
Get “low cost bus ticket” from the counter \~£7pp into Tokyo. Takes 1hr from bus platform 7\. They leave every 5-10mins.  
Please purchase a time-designated ticket at the LCB Ticket Counter located at each terminal building at Narita Airport and get to the bus stop at least 5 minutes before departure. At the ticket counter, you may pay with cash, transportation IC card (PASMO, Suica, etc.), or credit card. When boarding, staff will check your ticket, so please present it

**Day 10 – Saturday 24th October | Ine Fishing Village & Amanohashidate** 

**Car Rental:**  
Pick up: 8am (20min walk from accommodation)  
Nippon Rent-A-Car Nishi-Oji Sanjo  
24 Saiinkamiimadacho, Ukyo Ward, Kyoto, 615-0001, Japan

Return: 8pm

**Suggested Plan:**  
Drive to Amanohashidate for around 11am  
Take the chairlift/monorail up to Amanohashidate View Land. [https://www.viewland.jp/en/lift\_mono/](https://www.viewland.jp/en/lift_mono/)   
In October it is open 9:00–17:00, and the official site describes the view from the summit as the famous "flying dragon" view.  
12pm — Drive to Ine (about 45 minutes)  
The road follows the coast and the scenery gets increasingly rural as you approach the village.  
1pm — Park at Funaya no Sato Ine and walk into town as it’s not big enough for large cars  
It is a large, free car park on the hill above Ine.  
459 Kameshima, Ine, Yoza District, Kyoto 626-0424, Japan

13:15 — Walk the funaya waterfront  
The remarkable thing about Ine is that these aren't simply preserved historical buildings. Around 230 funaya remain along roughly 5 km of coastline, and many are still people's homes and working spaces.  
13:45 — Lunch at Ine Cafe — a good choice for something casual with the village atmosphere.  
Or Ine Restaurant Funaya for seafood

14:45 — Take a boat around Ine Bay \- [https://www.ine-kankou.jp/e\_active/small-boat-sea-taxi](https://www.ine-kankou.jp/e_active/small-boat-sea-taxi)   
Boat house tour could also be fun \- [https://www.ine-kankou.jp/e\_active/tomobutoya](https://www.ine-kankou.jp/e_active/tomobutoya) NEED CASH  
£5pp for boat, £3.50pp for house tour

15:30 — Coffee \+ explore  
16:00 — Start back to Kyoto

5 clustered are walkable, then the additional 2 need to drive to

Hells are only open from 8am–5pm   
Need to try the pudding  
![][image19]

### [https://whereandwander.com/first-timers-guide-to-beppu-hells-hot-springs-recommendations/](https://whereandwander.com/first-timers-guide-to-beppu-hells-hot-springs-recommendations/)

### [https://beppu-jigoku.com/pamphlet/images/English.pdf](https://beppu-jigoku.com/pamphlet/images/English.pdf) 

**Umi Jigoku:** a milky blue pool with strong venting steam.  
**Oniishibozu Jigoku**: a series of a small bubbling gray mud pools surrounded by volcanic rocks  
**Shiraike Jigoku**: a well landscaped milky white pond with a smaller aquarium.  
**Kamado Jigoku**: another spot with multiple blue, green, and red ponds with a large demon statue and food stalls selling food cooked by the steams. Shares similarities with Umi Jigoku. Book here to get your onsen cooked steam egg with entry.  
**Oniyama Jigoku**: a pond with very strong steam. The place is also home to a large number of caged crocodiles, which seems quite odd.  
**Chinoike Jigoku**: despite being named for a dramatic  red “blood pond,” it’s more of a dull orange. It also has a large gift shop like Umi and a full restaurant where you can get the hell-steamed food.  
**Tatsumaki Jigoku**: the only pond with a spouting geyser that erupts every 30–40 minutes.

**Beppu Ropeway**   
Views over Beppu \- one of the most beautiful sights in Japan in Autumn

10-7 Aza Kanbara Oaza Minami Tateishi, Beppu City, Oita, 874-0000

250 parking spaces

* **Tori No Ichi** \- an annual traditional Japanese festival held in November to pray for good fortune, health, and business prosperity.  
  A lantern-lit night that feels like stepping into old Edo, all grilled squid, hot sake and ornate lucky rakes.  
  3-5pm \- Best atmosphere after dark under the lanterns  
  **Location** \- Chokokuji Temple and Otori Shrine in Asakusa. 

  The signature item is the kumade — a decorative bamboo rake covered in lucky charms (koban gold coins, Okame masks, the Seven Gods of Fortune) meant to "rake in" wealth and luck.

  Eat everything. Yakisoba, takoyaki, grilled corn, chocolate bananas, hot sake in paper cups

Ben to leave around 8/9pm

**Day 25 – Sunday 8th November | Flights**

Checkout at 10am. Need to find somewhere to store bags.  
Leave accommodation around 2pm to get to Airport for 3:30/4. Can get the train or bus back.

![][image24] ![][image25]  

**Day 26 – Monday 9th November | Drive Home**

**Extra Details & Additional Information**

**Apps to Download**

* Tabelog \- Food rating app. Anything with a score of 3.5+ is going to be an excellent experience.   
* Klook \- for booking/booked experiences and some transport  
* Smart Ex App \- to book bullet train but must create an account. Easier to use Klook  
* Yamato \- Luggage Transfer  
* Google Maps  
* Google Translate with Japanese downloaded  
* Stamp Quest \- app for finding all stamps  
* Go \- Uber for Japan  
* Luup \- Electric scooter app  
* Suica \-  (only for Apple) Transport card  
* Uniqlo \- they have water filling stations  
* Line \- can get lots of discounts  
* Flush \- shows you all public toilets  
* Payke \- translation and shows you whats in products and has discounts

**Suggested Personal Flight Survival Kit**

* Wear \- Joggers, tshirt, jumper  
* Sliders  
* Pants \+ socks  
* Compression socks  
* Neck pillow  
* Eye mask  
* Footrest   
* Layers/Blanket  
* Passport  
* Cash  
* Itinerary  
* Notebook \+ pen  
* Snacks   
* Water  
* Cards  
* Book  
* Headphones  
* Films and TV downloaded  
* Power bank  
* Charging cables  
* Adaptor  
* Phone stand  
* Deodorant  
* Lip balm  
* Moisturiser  
* Hand sanitiser  
* Face wipes  
* Toothbrush and toothpaste  
* Paracetamol  
* Salt tablets  
* Plasters \+ waterproof   
* Poop bags for rubbish

**Packing List \-** [Japan 2026 - Packing List](https://docs.google.com/spreadsheets/d/1e-DINvKEhJGVDWHRux8yd8sh3Z3hVFILatizR2FtRhA/edit?usp=drive_link)

**Rules to Follow** 

* No tipping \- this is rude  
* Don't Jaywalk  
* Take rubbish home (bringing poop bags)  
* Take the receipt up to the till to pay, table paying isn't a thing  
* Don't show shoulders or clevage  
* Dont go with promoters or street sellers\!\!
